heroHeadline: Day 9,000 of America's Longest War — Russia-Taliban Military Pact Signed; TTP Eid Ceasefire; Jawid Niazi Day 23 in Taliban GDI; 24-Day Strike Pause
heroSubtitle: May 29, 2026 marks exactly 9,000 days since the US launched Operation Enduring Freedom on October 7, 2001 — America's longest-ever war, now in its 25th year. On Day 93 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq, Russia and the Taliban formalized a Military-Technical Cooperation Agreement signed at Moscow's International Security Forum (May 27-28) by Afghan Defense Minister Mohammad Yaqoob Mujahid and Russian Security Council Secretary Sergei Shoigu — Russia's first bilateral defense pact with Taliban-ruled Afghanistan. TTP leader Noor Wali Mehsud announced a 3-day Eid al-Adha ceasefire (10th–12th Dhu al-Hijjah, early June). Paigard News Agency director Jawid Niazi remained in Taliban GDI custody on Day 23 — no bail, no charges, no announced legal access. TOLOnews journalists Mansoor Niazi and Imran Danish remain in Afghanistan on bail pending trial after Eid. The 24-day pause in confirmed Pakistani cross-border airstrikes since the May 5 Dangam (Kunar) strike holds. WFP urgently needs $313 million as 4.9 million Afghan mothers and children face malnutrition — the 2026 UN appeal remains 60% unfunded. No formal ceasefire; no Urumqi Round 2 date; China silent on mediation since April 8.
